title: Canonical derived étale-localization comparisons
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $g:T\to S$ and $Y\xrightarrow{h}X$, $Y\xrightarrow{e}T$ form a chosen Cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]. Let $a:U\to X$, $b:B\to S$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $f_U:U\to B$ satisfy $fa=bf_U$. Work in the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of abelian sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with the exact inverse images and canonical derived adjunctions of [sbc-def-base-change-map]. For any commuting square, define $\alpha^D$ by applying the canonical inverse-image square comparison termwise and descending it through the localization, with the canonical composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. For a square $hd=ah_U$, define $p^D: a^{-1}Rh_*\to Rh_{U*}d^{-1}$ as the adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $(\alpha^D)^{-1}$ under $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ and $h_U^{-1}\dashv Rh_{U*}$. Put $T_B=B\times_ST$, $Y_U=U\times_XY$, and use the canonical local arrow $e_U:Y_U\to T_B$ and Cartesian local square constructed in [lem-sbc-base-change-arrow-localization]. The canonical source and target localization comparison transformations are $C_L^D=f_U^{-1}(p^D_g)\circ\alpha^D_f$ and $C_R^D=Rh_{U*}(\alpha^D_e)\circ p^D_h$, respectively, with the indicated functor associators. Here $p^D_g$ uses $T_B\to T$, $B\to S$, and $p^D_h$ uses $Y_U\to Y$, $U\to X$. Inverse image along an etale map is identified with restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. These are defined transformations, with no arbitrary comparison datum supplied; their invertibility is a property to be established subsequently.
